description: Hi! I'm Jana Zakaria, a 14-year-old solo innovator passionate about aerospace engineering, physics, mathematics, and coding. As an active participant in international science and writing competitions, I love breaking down complex scientific theories and turning official NASA data into real, impactful solutions through my project, AEGIS-X.
summary: AEGIS-X is a research intelligence platform designed to make NASA's microgravity combustion research easier to explore and understand. Focused on the BASS-II investigation, it organizes experimental records, distinguishes original measurements from curated data, and helps users examine potential record relationships and data-quality issues. By combining data exploration, source traceability, and careful reconciliation in one workspace, AEGIS-X aims to make complex space research more accessible while preserving scientific accuracy and uncertainty.
details:
What We Built

AEGIS-X is a browser-based microgravity combustion research intelligence platform unifying all 51 official NASA BASS-II experimental records (PMMA Table 5.1 & SIBAL Table 7.1) from NASA/TM-20210011385 into an interactive, traceable workspace.

Main Features

- Mission Overview: Introduces the unified repository and core scientific governance principles.

- Advanced Matrix & Correlation: Cross-references SIBAL airflow speeds with PMMA regression rates, highlighting a critical non-linear oxygen propagation threshold between 18.5 vol% and 22.2 vol%.

- Telemetry Observatory: Provides statistical summaries and distribution breakdowns across all 51 unified BASS-II records.

- 51-Record NASA Master Database: Offers live search and filtering across complete experimental logs with direct source lineage.

Innovation and Scientific Integrity

AEGIS-X combines data fusion, anomaly correlation, and strict source provenance in one interface. It enforces a clear separation between verified NASA flight measurements and analytical interpretations.

Intended Impact

The platform makes complex microgravity combustion data accessible to researchers and students, supporting safer material selection for future Lunar and Mars habitats as well as closed environments on Earth.

Original Idea and Development

AEGIS-X originated as my own original idea, inspired by my passion for NASA, space exploration, and microgravity combustion physics. I designed the concept, defined its scientific direction, and built the platform using AI tools (Google Gemini, Toolipedia, and Gamma) as technical assistants to accelerate implementation and presentation design.
